title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Washington and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels show the winery, grape, AVA and vintage. Washington uses US federal rules for AVAs, 85%, and vintage, 95%, but requires 85% for a named grape, stricter than the federal 75%. Columbia Valley is the broadest AVA; Red Mountain or Walla Walla are more specific. Many wineries are in Woodinville but source grapes from the east.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Washington Cabernet suits steak, lamb and burgers; Merlot suits roast pork and duck; Syrah suits barbecue, lamb and game; Riesling suits Asian food, seafood and spicy dishes. Pacific Northwest salmon suits lighter reds and Chardonnay. Serve reds at 16 to 18 degrees, Riesling at 7 to 10.
steps.highlight: Cabernet with steak, Riesling with spice

steps.prompt: Which Washington AVA is famous for savoury Syrah from cobblestones?

steps.body: Woodinville, near Seattle, has over 100 tasting rooms, but most grapes are grown three to four hours east, across the Cascades.
